that population. **Under the struck reading (i) at *n* ≥ 8 and under reading (ii) always it is
exactly zero, at which point the rule is unshipped whatever the code says.** **Criterion 9 fails the
wave if the chosen combination empties it.**

### E10 — the dishwasher: the corner path is the majority, and adjacency is width-neutral

**[measured, HEAD, no dishwasher composed]** Where a 600 mm dishwasher could abut the sink, counting
a composed storage slot as convertible and a core role or a tall column as not:

| | Rooms | Share |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| a convertible slot on the sink's **own wall** | 13 860 | **6.6 %** |
| a convertible slot **across the corner** | 102 141 | **48.3 %** |
| either — the machine can abut | 116 001 | 54.8 % |
| neither — under Q-D1's rule it is **dropped** | 95 550 | 45.2 % |
| …of those, a slot exists elsewhere in the kitchen and adjacency forbids it | 33 150 | 15.7 % |

**Two things follow, and both change the charter's shape.**

1. **The owner's 2026-09-15 across-the-corner ruling is not a rescue clause; it carries 88 % of the
   dishwasher's placements** (102 141 of 116 001). The charter calls it *"the most likely source of
   surprise"* and that is an understatement: **the same-wall case alone would place a dishwasher in
   6.6 % of kitchens.** *(The cause is structural and worth stating once: on wall B the spatial array
   is `[storage…, core reversed]`, so wall B's **corner-most** body is a storage slot whenever B has
   one, and a sink on B is separated from wall A by all of them. `generation-priorities.ts:182-198`.)*
2. **Taken as a conversion of an adjacent storage slot, the dishwasher changes no width, no tile, no
   remainder and no block threshold.** D7's *"it consumes 600 mm of the run, so 7D3's D2.2 block table
   moves by exactly one module"* is true of the dishwasher-as-a-new-core-role and **false of the
   dishwasher-as-a-conversion** — and the conversion is what the adjacency rule actually asks for.
   **This is D15.5/H4's lesson a second time**: a measurement of the plan's internal quantities is not
   a measurement of the product. **It also removes the dishwasher from the set D11 grouped into this
   wave**, since that grouping was *"what re-baselines the run's arithmetic"*.

**Recommendation to the coordinator, and it is a scheduling call rather than a ruling: take the
dishwasher out of 7D5 and give it its own wave.** It shares no re-baselining with the width work
(finding 2), its hard part is a **placement** constraint that crosses the corner and that no rule in
7D1–7D4 has ever expressed (finding 1), and 7D5 is already the largest width change in the
milestone. **S5 below is written so it can be lifted out whole.** **This plan does not make the
call** and does not overturn D11; D11 grouped the dishwasher with the cargo on an argument this
measurement has removed the premise from, and that is put back to the coordinator rather than decided
here.

### The goal, and what is out

**Goal: compose the owner's run order astride the hob** — the bottle cabinet right of the hob, the
second drawer cabinet left of it, the third drawer clause resolved under the owner's answer to Q-H5,
the block threshold table re-measured, and `PAN_DRAWER_BASE_BUILD_ID` given the caller 7D4 kept it
for.

**And one thing the goal is NOT, restated after Q-H3's answer because it was the wave's headline
until 2026-09-16: reaching the owner's proportion is not this wave's measure of success.** The
proportion governs **3.03 % of placed kitchens** (E1) and its ceiling in half of those is **geometric
rather than a rule choice** (E8.1). **What this wave is actually worth is the positional order, which
touches every kitchen**: a bottle cabinet beside the hob, a second drawer type in the run, and the
cooking group standing together. **A close-out that leads with a percentage will be leading with the
smaller half**, and criterion 3 is written to stop it.

**In scope:** `src/generation/generation-priorities.ts`, `src/generation/body-choice.ts`,
`src/run-end-panel.ts` (one comment), and the domain, parity and adversarial suites that cover them.
**Out of scope, named so the boundary is a decision:** the corner body (C2 — there is no insertable
corner row at all); the top row (E11); the wall row (D8); any ratio constant anywhere (G6, H7);
`chooseWallCut`'s keying; the *"Perete A"* field copy.

### Module boundaries

- **`body-choice.ts` stays a pure leaf.** It gains the bottle cabinet's build id and **no width, no
  position and no threshold**. It already refuses to export a drawer/door classifier (F7) and writes
  no id (F8); both hold. **`base-bottle-cargo`'s 200/300 set and its price gap are the catalogue's
  and the price book's** (`catalog.ts:201-213`, `sample-price-book.ts:109`) — a generation-side copy
  of either is ADR 0102's second authority.
- **`generation-priorities.ts` owns the order.** Which body stands where in the group, and the
  arithmetic that decides whether an optional member is affordable, are facts about the run, the wall
  cut and the corner — and this module holds all three. **It must not learn a proportion.**
- **`tall-end-rule.ts` and `leftover-rule.ts` are not edited.** The block table moves because the
  core's width moves; that is E3's design and is why the table is *derivable*. **A wave that edits a
  threshold literal in `tall-end-rule.ts` has misunderstood this.**

### Slices, each with an owner

**S0 — the inherited comment, and one obligation that is already discharged.** *(Owner: 7D5's first
implementer. No behaviour changes; Tier: none, reviewed with S1.)*

1. **`run-end-panel.ts:94-98` — rewrite the stated reason.** The veto is correct; *"a fitter closes
   that gap with a filler strip"* is a sentence about a physical wall that ADR 0120 Amendment D1
   removed. The replacement states the run reading: the panel's outer face may not pass the **run**
   the customer asked to furnish, and there is no wall beyond it to model. **Cite ADR 0120 D2.
   Comment-only — a behaviour change here is a defect.**
2. **The ADR 0091 Amendment A pointer is ALREADY THERE and must not be re-done.** The 7D4 close-out
   records it as owed and *"verified at HEAD: the comment at `:221-226` … names no file"*. **Re-read
   at `ffc472e`: `qa-7d3-tall-end-block.adversarial.test.ts:228-232` names
   `tests/generation/drawer-rows.test.ts` and quotes the assertion at `:316`.** The obligation was
   discharged after that sentence was written. **S0 verifies the pointer still resolves and records
   that it does; it writes nothing.** *(ADR 0119 decision 4 working: a dated obligation re-read at
   HEAD before being acted on.)*

**S1 — the bottle cabinet.** *(Owner: implementer. Tier: Full.)* The 300 mm `base-bottle-cargo`
stands immediately right of the hob in the **reading** order, and is **dropped rather than allowed to
refuse a kitchen or to drop a core role** (E3). Its neighbours are asserted, never the cargo
(risk 11). **The head comment records why it is safe — `plannedVoid` accepts a wider opening at the
same start — and not the false reason H5 gives (E4).**

**S2 — the second drawer cabinet.** *(Owner: implementer. Tier: Full.)* A 600 mm
`PAN_DRAWER_BASE_BUILD_ID` immediately left of the hob, under the owner's answer to Q-H6. **This is
the slice that gives the constant its caller**, discharging the note 7D4 wrote at
`body-choice.ts:54-62`. **Two deep pan drawers beside the hob is the body's own reason for standing
there**; the pairing with the preparation cabinet's `base-3drawer` is what lets the group carry two
types, which is R2's *"maximum cabinet types"* satisfied by placement rather than by a cycle.

**Q-H3's answer added candidate C to this slice's question and it changes the slice's blast radius,
not its code.** Under C the module is composed only where *D* ≥ 6 — **6 411 rooms rather than 84 291**
— and the kitchen at or above the threshold is **identical** to candidate A's (E7.1). **The
engineering consequence is criterion 9's**: C leaves 4 260 of D15.7's 6 660 discriminating rooms
standing where A leaves 660. **S2 is implemented so the condition is one predicate**, so that the
choice between A and C is a one-line change after the owner answers and not a re-write.

**S3 — the threshold rule.** *(Owner: implementer. Tier: Full. **Blocked on Q-H5**, and on nothing
else.)* **Re-scoped by Q-H3's answer.** The owner's *"2 are drawers"* is a rule over the plain
cabinets at *D* ≥ 6, and **7D4 already supplies the first of the two in 100 % of that population**
(E8). So the slice is: **count *D* after the bottle cabinet stands, and where it reaches six, give a
second plain cabinet a drawer body.** **Width-neutral if the second drawer cabinet is not already in
the group and a second plain cabinet stands after the hob — which is true in 48.84 % of the
population and false in the other 51.16 %, measured** (E8.1). **Under reading (ii) it instead inserts
a 600 mm module and moves E5's table again.** ~~Reading (i)'s gate~~ is **struck** (E8) and must not
be built. **The slice is written after the answer, not before.**

**Two things S3 must not do, both because a criterion already forbids them.** It must not require two
drawers where only one plain cabinet stands after the hob — unsatisfiable by correct output in 3 280
rooms (criterion 6). And it must not put a drawer in a wall-B slot between the fridge and the sink to
make the count — **the owner's own order rules those door cabinets** (H2), and 4–5 of the six are
there in every threshold room.

**S4 — the re-baselining.** *(Owner: implementer + QA. Tier: Full.)* 7D3's criterion 12 restated
against 7D5's own planner **and the restatement recorded in ADR 0110** — not an edited 7D3
assertion, which `docs/WORKFLOW.md` calls a defect. E5's block table and E6's absorb count written
into the record. **Risk 2 below is this slice's.**

**S5 — the dishwasher.** *(Owner: unassigned pending the coordinator's call on E10. Tier: Full.)*
Written last and severable. If it stays: the machine takes an **adjacent composed storage slot**, on
the sink's own wall or across the corner, and is dropped where neither exists — 45.2 % of rooms
(E10). **Q-D1's ranking question stays theoretical only if the same-wall case is rare, and it is:
6.6 %.** If it goes to its own wave, S5 lifts out whole and nothing above it changes.

### Acceptance criteria

**Each criterion names the population that discriminates it and that population's size (ADR 0121
decision 5), and each names the sabotage that discharges decision 3 in both directions: (a) remove
the behaviour, leave the correlate standing, the check must go red; (b) move the correlate, leave the
behaviour standing, the check must stay green.**

1. *(unit, boundary)* **The bottle cabinet stands immediately right of the hob in the reading order,
   and nowhere else.** Witness **6300 × 4700**, wall A reads
   `sink, base-3drawer, base-hob-2drawer, base-bottle-cargo, …`. **Discriminating population: the
   59 580 rooms (28.2 %) whose sink is on wall B, and within them the hob-on-B rooms, where the
   reading order runs against the spatial one — a rule written for wall A puts the cargo on the wrong
   side of the hob and no count, width, remainder or digest moves.** *(This plan's own model made
   exactly that error; see E0.)* **Must not:** the cargo adjacent to another cargo, or at an index
   derived from a wall literal rather than from `isLaidOutInReverse`.
   **(a)** delete the cargo from the group and leave `BOTTLE_CARGO_BUILD_ID` exported → red.
   **(b)** change the constant's value to another catalogue id while the composer still emits one
   cargo right of the hob → **green**, because no assertion may ask the composer for the answer.

2. *(sweep)* **No room that generates a kitchen today fails to generate one after this wave.**
   Measured over all 211 551 placed rooms: `minimumMet` may not go false in any of them, and
   `dropped` may not gain a member in any of them. **Discriminating population: the 6 300 rooms at
   wall A 900–2390 that the unconditional bottle cabinet refuses (E3), and the 16 800 in which it
   would take a core role.** **An aggregate placement count is not evidence here** — 205 251 of
   211 551 is 97.0 % and reads as success.
   **(a)** remove the conditional drop and compose the cargo unconditionally → red, naming a witness
   room. **(b)** change which body the group's optional member is → green.

3. *(sweep, on the owner's *D*; **branch on Q-H4 and Q-H3a**)* **The threshold population, and what
   the kitchen gets in it, are reported and pinned — and no criterion asserts that a ratio is met.**
   The population is **the rooms with *D* ≥ 6 once the bottle cabinet is placed: 6 411 of 211 551,
   3.03 %**, split **5 140 at *D* = 6 and 1 271 at *D* = 7**, and *D* reaches **no higher anywhere in
   the approved range**. Within it: **7D4 ships exactly one drawer in 100 % of those rooms**; this
   wave's minimum reaches **two drawers in 48.84 % (3 131 rooms), mean 1.488**; Q-H5 reading (ii)
   reaches **61.63 %, mean 1.616**. **Must not:** a ratio constant, or any assertion that drawers
   divided by cabinets meets one third — G6 and H7 stand. **Must not:** a criterion that reports the
   proportion as an aggregate over all placed rooms; **the discriminating population is 3.03 % of the
   sweep and an aggregate hides it entirely.**
   **(a)** delete the threshold and let the rule fire everywhere → red, on a room with *D* = 5.
   **(b)** change *which* drawer body stands in a threshold slot → green.

4. *(sweep, **branch on Q-H3a**)* **The threshold population is re-measured after the wave, not
   carried from this plan.** *D*'s mean falls from **2.028** at HEAD to **1.814** once the bottle
   cabinet stands, and the *D* ≥ 6 population falls from **9 501 (4.49 %)** to **6 411 (3.03 %)** —
   **the wave's own bodies shrink the population its headline rule governs by a third**, and the
   close-out says so rather than reporting the proportion alone (D15.5's guard). **If Q-H3a is
   answered *the preparation cabinet counts*, the population is 22 091 (10.44 %) and every figure in
   criterion 3 is re-taken over that set, not re-labelled.**

5. *(unit)* **`PAN_DRAWER_BASE_BUILD_ID` has a production caller.** `body-choice.ts:54-62`'s note
   that *"generation places it nowhere in this wave"* is struck and replaced with where it now
   stands. **Must not:** the note deleted without a replacement sentence — ADR 0091 Amendment A's
   rule about a claim that is retired rather than moved.

6. *(unit, the two witnesses the rule needs, and **branch on Q-H4**)* **The threshold rule is asserted
   at one room where two drawers are reachable and one where they are not** — because the population
   is two shapes and **a witness from either alone reads as the rule working or as the rule broken**
   (E8.1). **Reachable: 6000 × 4100** — *D* = 6 as **A2 / B4**, three columns, wall A reads
   `sink, base-3drawer, base-hob-2drawer, base-bottle-cargo, base-3drawer, base-cabinet, tall-oven-tower, tall-pantry, tall-pantry`;
   **1 860 rooms (29.01 %) share this shape.** **Unreachable: 3610 × 4700** — *D* = 6 as **A1 / B5**,
   no block, wall A reads `sink, base-3drawer, base-hob-oven, base-bottle-cargo, base-3drawer`, and
   **the single plain cabinet after the hob is already the drawer**; **3 280 rooms (51.16 %) share it,
   and they are the majority of the population the rule governs.** **Must not:** a criterion that
   requires two drawers at *D* ≥ 6 unconditionally — it is unsatisfiable by correct output in those
   3 280 rooms, which is the defect class 7D4's plan shipped five of. **If Q-H4 is answered *yes*, the
   unreachable witness is 3610 × 4700 still — its hob is `base-hob-oven`, so it gains nothing — while
   6000 × 4100 gains two fronts; the pair keeps discriminating.**
   **(a)** delete the threshold rule and leave the constants → red on 6000 × 4100.
   **(b)** swap which of `base-3drawer` / `base-panbank` stands in each slot → green.

7. *(sweep)* **The block threshold table is the one E5 measures for the chosen candidate**, re-taken
   after the slice rather than derived by adding 300 or 600 to 7D3's. **Discriminating population: the
   rooms within one 10 mm step of each boundary.** **Must not:** a threshold literal edited in
   `tall-end-rule.ts` — the table follows the core's width and moves by itself.

**What this wave is, in one sentence.** The owner's *"on wider wall you always place the sink and

constant `PREFIX_WALL = "B"`.**

#### E0.2 — the falsification that makes the rest of this plan admissible

**Claim: no preference computed inside `chooseWallCut` can satisfy the owner's rule in a B-wider
room. [source-verified, then measured]**

`GENERATION_PRIORITIES` is **fridge → sink → preparation → hob** (`generation-priorities.ts:34-44`);
`builtPlan` sends `kept.slice(0, cut)` to wall **B** and `kept.slice(cut)` to wall **A**
(`:150-151`), and `PREFIX_WALL` is the literal `"B"` (`:20`). So the five reachable cuts are:

| cut | wall B gets | wall A gets |
| ---: | --- | --- |
| 0 | — | fridge, sink, preparation, hob |
| 1 | fridge | sink, preparation, hob |
| 2 | fridge, sink | preparation, hob |
| 3 | fridge, sink, preparation | hob |
| 4 | fridge, sink, preparation, hob | — |

With **B** the wider wall the rule needs `fridge ∈ A` **and** `sink, hob ∈ B`. The fridge is the
order's **first** element, so `fridge ∈ A` forces `cut = 0` — which puts the sink and the hob on A
with it. **The rule is unreachable at every cut index, for any preference function whatsoever.**

**Falsified rather than argued.** A variant that ranks the feasible cuts **lexicographically by rule
compliance** — hob on the wider wall, then sink on the wider wall, then fridge on the narrower, and
only then today's `|cut − preferred|` tie-break — produces output **identical on every one of the
8 615 rooms** of the 50 mm sweep to the plain re-keying below. **The preference was never the binding
constraint**, and a wave that spends its budget there will find the same thing at the end instead of
the start.

**This corrects the brief that commissioned this plan, and the correction is recorded rather than
absorbed.** The dispatch asked for *"the wave that fixes `chooseWallCut`'s wall-identity keying"* and
described the defect as `preferred` being *"a cut index"* with `capacities` entering *"only as a
feasibility filter … never as a preference"*. **Every one of those statements is true, and the
conclusion a reader draws from them — that the fix is to make capacities enter as a preference — is
false.** The correction is not a quibble about scope: **a wave dispatched on the brief's framing would
have shipped a preference computation, measured its split, and found 100 % on one arm and 21.2 % on
the other, which is the state it was sent to fix.** Recorded here because **the next person to read
this module will reach for the comparator too** — it is the part that looks wrong — and because ADR
0121 decision 4's *"the expected value comes from outside the producer"* applies to a brief exactly as
it does to a test.

### E1 — the key: the entered wall length, not the free run, and the split is what proves it

**Two candidate keys exist and they disagree. [measured]** The **entered wall length**
(`room.widthMm` against `room.depthMm`) and the **free run capacity** (`runs.A` against `runs.B`
width — the entered length less the corner's reach, **900 mm on A and 1000 mm on B**) rank the walls
differently in **3 861 of 211 551 placed rooms (1.83 %)**: every room whose entered lengths differ by
less than 100 mm. At 50 mm the same divergence is **213 rooms (2.5 %)**.

**Both were implemented and swept, and the result is the wave's central instrument. [measured]**

| the code is keyed on → | hob on the wider wall, split by **entered length** | hob on the wider wall, split by **free run** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **free run capacity** | 95.7 % / 100.0 % | **100.0 % / 100.0 %** |
| **entered wall length** | **100.0 % / 100.0 %** | 98.7 % / 100.0 % |

**The split that reads 100 / 100 names the key.** This is ADR 0121 decision 5 turned into a cheap,
two-sided falsification: the wave does not merely report a split, it reports **two** splits and shows
which one the code actually answers. A criterion that reads 100 / 100 on *both* has discriminated
nothing.

**Ruled: the key is the entered wall length.** Two reasons, and the second is the durable one.
(1) It is the quantity the owner's sentence names — *"wider wall"* — and, under **ADR 0120 Amendment
C1**, the entered number **is** the run the customer chose to furnish, so it is a decision they made
rather than a measurement the product derived. (2) The corner's reach is a fact about the corner, not
about which wall is wider; keying on capacity would make *"which wall is wider"* mean something no
customer can compute from the two numbers they typed. **The 1.83 % is recorded here because it is
exactly the population a later reader will "fix" in the other direction**, and doing so without a
dated record would reopen this.

### E3 — the tall block moves, and ADR 0110 Amendment E says it may not

**This is the finding most likely to be missed, because nothing about it is visible in
`generation-priorities.ts`.** Amendment E rules that the full-height block stands at the free end of
**wall A** *"and nowhere else"*, and `tall-end-rule.ts:51-53` states the reason at the parameter
itself: *"wall A's free end is the only site an L run has, so a hob on wall B means no block and a hob
that keeps its oven."* **[source-verified]**

**That reason is about the free end the layout leaves, not about the letter A.** Wall B's spatial
array is `[storage…, core reversed]`, so B's free end holds core bodies and has no leftover modules to
swap for columns. Re-keyed, that is true of whichever wall carries the **prefix** — and the block's
site becomes the **suffix** wall's free end, which is wall B in every B-wider room.

**Measured, 10 mm, 211 551 placed. [measured]**

| | blocks | on wall A | on wall B | hob keeps its own oven |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| **HEAD** | 110 591 (52.28 %) | 110 591 | 0 | 47.72 % |
| **the block follows the suffix wall** | **144 866 (68.48 %)** | 97 691 | **47 175 (22.3 % of placed)** | 31.52 % |
| **the block is confined to physical wall A** | 97 691 (46.18 %) | 97 691 | 0 | 53.82 % |

**12 826** rooms would carry a block on wall B where HEAD carries one on wall A. **Confining the block
costs 12 900 rooms a block they have today** — a regression nobody asked for, arriving as a side
effect of a rule about sinks.

~~**Ruled for this plan, and it is a recommendation the amendment must ratify rather than a decision
this plan may take alone: the block follows the suffix wall.**~~ **SUPERSEDED within the day, and by

**ADR 0110 Amendment E's *"and nowhere else"* is OVERTURNED by that ruling**, with those two figures
as its authority. **The engineering argument is kept and demoted to what it always was** — a reason,
not a permission: E's stated reason was about *the free end the layout leaves* rather than about the
letter A, so following the run honours E's intent while confining it would be a regression nobody
asked for. **The owner did not need that argument to rule, and the ruling does not rest on it.**

**What this changes in the plan: slice S1(a) now writes an amendment instead of waiting for one, and
S2 is no longer gated on an owner answer.** The sequence is unchanged and still binding — **S1(a)
lands before S2 writes a line of code** — but it is now a documentation-before-code discipline rather
than a dispatch gate. **A wave that ships the block on wall B without that record has still silently
overturned a standing ruling**, which `AGENTS.md` forbids whether or not the overturning was
authorised.

### E4 — the run reads the other way in the mirrored rooms, and the owner has accepted it

**ADR 0110 Amendment A1, quoted:** *"On a left-corner L the run reads from wall B's free end toward
the corner and then along wall A from the corner outward"*, and the order itself is *"along the run,
left to right as seen from inside the room"*. **[doc-quoted]**

Re-keyed, a B-wider room reads from **wall A's** free end toward the corner and out along **wall B**.
The bodies, the widths and the cooking sequence along the run are unchanged; **the run's direction in
the room is mirrored.** It is visible even where only one wall is furnished — at **900 × 3500**, C2's
own worked counterexample, reproduced here:

| | wall B, corner outward |
| --- | --- |
| **HEAD** | hob → preparation → sink → fridge |
| **re-keyed** | fridge → sink → preparation → hob |

**Both put all four bodies on wall B** (wall A at 900 mm has no free run at all), so neither is more
compliant — **what changes is which end the cooking order starts at.** **[measured]**

~~**This plan does not treat it as a defect** … so it is **Q-7D8-1** below and it is the owner's, not
the coordinator's.~~ **ANSWERED the same day: the owner was shown the 900 × 3500 case above —
`hob, prep, sink, fridge` becoming `fridge, sink, prep, hob` corner-outward, same bodies, same widths
— and ACCEPTED IT.**

**And it is not a concession: the owner had already described this arrangement in their own words,
which is the sentence to quote at the keying site rather than this plan's reasoning about it:**

> *"sometimes the arrangement is in mirror, like hub, cabinets (drawers), sink, cabinets, fridge"*

~~**So ADR 0110 Amendment A1's *"left to right as seen from inside the room"* is RESTATED, not
broken**~~, ***and that verdict was too tidy. CORRECTED 2026-09-16 by S1(a), which is now written and
committed at `2439da5` as [ADR 0110 Amendment I](../decisions/0110-generation-inserts-through-the-command-path-and-the-corner-is-structural-data.md).
The coordinator asked S1's author to judge whether "restated, not broken" was honest or merely
convenient, and to say so if it was convenient. It was. **The verdict splits three ways:***

- ***A1's ORDER is genuinely restated.*** The owner's sentence lists hob-first and fridge-last — the
  exact reverse of A1's written direction, offered as normal. That is the owner narrowing their own
  earlier *"from left to right"*, by the only authority that could.
- ***A1's SECOND SENTENCE is BROKEN, and is recorded as corrected rather than restated.***
  *"On a left-corner L the run reads from wall B's free end toward the corner and then along wall A
  from the corner outward"* (`0110:124`) is stated **unqualifiedly**, with the reference kitchen
  following as corroboration rather than as a scope limit. After this wave it is **false in 82 395 of
  211 551 placed rooms**. Amendment I corrects it to *the prefix wall's free end*.
- ***"left to right as seen from inside the room" had two readings this record never separated:***
  along the run — untouched, and it governs — and as a direction in the room, which **is** broken in
  the mirrored population. Amendment I resolves the ambiguity explicitly so the next reader cannot
  resolve it the other way.

**What survives unchanged is the sentence below**, and it is why the wave is still sound: A1 describes the run's order **along the run**; it does
not fix which end of the room the run begins at, and the owner's sentence says so independently of
this wave. **A later reader must not find a mirrored kitchen and treat it as A1 violated** — the
amendment exists to stop exactly that reading, and the owner's sentence is its authority.

**What this changes in the plan: nothing measured, and one gate removed.** Every figure in E0–E8 was
taken before the ruling and none of them moves; the ruling chose between two behaviours this plan had
already measured. **S1(a) and therefore S2 are ungated.**

### E5 — what the corrected rule reaches, with every exception class named and sized

**Re-keyed on the entered wall length, 10 mm, excluding the 351 equal-wall rooms. [measured]**

| | A wider (128 805) | B wider (82 395) | exceptions |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| **hob on the wider wall** | **128 805 / 128 805** | **82 395 / 82 395** | **0** |
| sink on the wider wall | — | — | **14 335 (6.78 % of placed)** |
| fridge on the narrower wall | — | — | 31 640 (14.96 %), plus 28 785 (13.61 %) with no fridge at all |

**The hob's arm is exactly zero on both sides, so it is written as a must-not and never as a
percentage.** The hob is the reading order's last element, so it leaves the suffix wall only at
`cut = kept.length`, which the preference reaches only when the suffix wall cannot hold the hob alone
— and no room in the accepted range does that.

**The sink's 14 335 are the priority ladder, not a preference defect, and the distinction decides a
criterion.** **3 595** of them are rooms whose wider wall has **under 1 200 mm** of free run and
cannot hold a sink and a hob at all. The other **10 740** have a wider wall holding two of the three
suffix bodies but not all three: the cut moves to 2, the sink crosses to the narrower wall, and **the
fridge and the preparation cabinet are both kept.** Dropping the preparation cabinet instead would
satisfy the rule and costs almost nothing in width — the leftover rule refills the same 600 mm with a
storage cabinet — **but ADR 0110 A3 orders the drops (storage, then the fridge, then the preparation
cabinet) and the owner's new sentence says *"always"* about the sink and the hob. Nobody has ruled
which wins.** That is **Q-7D8-2**, and **this plan is written for *the ladder wins*: a rule about which
wall a body stands on may never cause a body to be dropped.**

### E6 — the 4-metre relaxation is a permission this wave never needs to exercise

**Held apart from Amendment B1's four metres, per ADR 0120 Amendment C3, and the separation is
restated here because this is the first wave to act on either.** B1 is a **market judgement** about
whom to optimise for and **narrows no bound** (B2). C's clause is a **geometric threshold** for when
the layout rule relaxes. **Neither implies the other, and *"the owner said 4 metres, so above that we
do not have to care"* is the sentence both halves exist to refuse.**

**Measured, 10 mm. [measured]** **25 190 of 211 551 placed rooms (11.91 %) have both entered walls
over 4 000 mm**, **5 995** of them B-wider. Read against the **free run** instead of the entered
length the population collapses to **1 400 (0.66 %)** — a second, independent reason to key the whole
wave on the entered length (E1).

**And in all 25 190 of them, the corrected generator already stands the fridge on the narrower wall,
and in none of them is the fridge dropped.** Above 4 000 mm on both walls the narrower wall offers at
least 3 000 mm of free run and a 700 mm fridge always fits, so the cut never collapses.

**So the relaxation is satisfied by doing nothing, and a `> 4000` branch would be dead code.** It
enters this plan as a **must-not** (criterion 9) plus **one line at the keying site saying that the
clause's absence is the rule being satisfied**, so that a later reader does not see no `4000` literal
and conclude the ruling was never implemented. **The trigger that would make the branch live, recorded
in ADR 0118's shape and not built for: a later ruling that lets this rule drop a body (Q-7D8-2
answered the other way), at which point above 4 m becomes the region where it must not.**

### E7 — risk 21 verified from source: right about the rule, and its summary is dangerous about the code

fridge → sink → preparation → hob, and **no re-keying of which wall carries the prefix changes it.**

**But *"does not need to change 7D4's rule"* is not *"does not touch 7D4's code."* Four sites spell

| `:312-314` | `isLaidOutInReverse(wall) { return wall === PREFIX_WALL; }` | the single answer behind **both** reversals |
| `:293-298` | `firstStorageSlotAfterTheHob` reads `slotsInReadingOrder("B", …)` then `("A", …)` | that is **prefix then suffix**, spelled as two wall letters |
| `:243` | `` id: `column:A:${String(index)}` `` | the block's id hard-codes wall A, and columns stand on B in **47 175** rooms (E3) |

while **no count, width, remainder, cut, provenance or digest moves**, and `buildId` on a composed
slot is precisely the field the 7D3 baseline masks. **So the obligation to carry forward is not
*"re-measure the split"* but *"re-key four sites, one of which nothing in this repository can
catch"*** — which is why criterion 7 exists and why it is a dedicated assertion rather than a
baseline row.

**Risk 21's re-measurement, discharged here. [measured]** D15.7's split moves from **53 751 (25.41 %)
on wall A and 6 660 (3.15 %) on wall B** to **50 361 (23.81 %) and 5 910 (2.79 %)**. ~~**The wall-B
discriminating arm shrinks by 11.3 % and does not empty**, so 7D4's wall-B witnesses stay reachable

> **CORRECTED 2026-09-17 — this paragraph measured one population and reasoned about another, and

>

**The recommendation is 7D8 first, and it is not close. Four reasons, in the order of their
weight.**

**1. 7D5's plan is stated in populations this wave moves, so running 7D5 first means measuring it

| --- | ---: | ---: |

**E9 chose candidate C over candidate A specifically because C keeps 4 260 of that 6 660** — *"6.5×
the discriminating population"*. **That denominator is about to move.** Choosing between candidates on
a number that changes under a wave you have already decided to run is the error ADR 0121 decision 5
exists to prevent, one level up.

**2. They cannot be in flight together in either order, so the choice is which is second, not
whether.** Both edit `generation-priorities.ts`, and **both invalidate
`tests/generation/7d3-composition-baseline.json`.** Whichever runs second re-captures the artefact

**3. Scale, and the owner's own words.** This defect is a rule **the owner has already given** and it
is wrong in **38.95 %** of room shapes — the arm where it is wrong reads **0.0 %** compliance on the
fridge. 7D5's headline rule binds in **3.03 %** of kitchens, and 7D5's own E8.1 records that its second
drawer has nowhere to stand in half of those. **7D5's plan says this itself, in its own voice:** *"it
is an argument against letting the proportion set this wave's priorities."* The larger, already-ruled
change goes underneath the smaller, partly-unanswered one.

**4. They do not conflict logically, in either order, and one fragile-looking 7D5 fact was checked

wall** the run's prefix lands on. Neither restates the other's rule. The fact worth checking was 7D5's

**Measured: in the *D* ≥ 6 population the hob stands on physical wall A in 100.00 % of rooms under

**The honest case for the other order, stated so the coordinator is not agreed with by default.**
7D5 is planned, measured and dispatchable **today**; this wave is not planned until this section

### The goal, and what is out

**Goal: the wall that carries the reading order's prefix is derived from the entered wall lengths, so
that the sink and the hob stand on the wider wall and the fridge on the narrower — by construction,
on both sides of the split, rather than by correlation on one.**

**Out of this wave, and named so they are not absorbed:**

- **The reading order itself.** ADR 0110 A1's fridge → sink → preparation → hob is untouched, as is
  7D4's rule stated in it (E7). **No criterion in this wave may assert anything about which body
  fills a storage slot.**
- **Widths.** This wave composes no new body and changes no declared width. Width work is 7D5's.
- **The corner's reach** (7D6) and **the corner builders** (7D7). This wave reads `lShellFloorRuns`
  and changes nothing beneath it.
- **The *"Perete A"* field copy**, which ADR 0120 Amendment D makes more load-bearing and which
  remains **unowned**. It is a different defect in the same amendment and is not smuggled in here.
- ~~**The two first-slice chores 7D4 handed to *"7D5's first slice"***~~ — **there is one, and it is
  in scope here if this wave runs first.** 7D4 assigned two; **the ADR 0091 Amendment A pointer is
  already discharged at `ffc472e` and was verified at HEAD by this plan, not relayed** — see slice S4,
  which carries the line numbers. What remains is `run-end-panel.ts:94-98`'s false comment reason, and
  **7D8 has a particular claim on it because R7 sends an implementer into that same module.** The
  scheduling call is still the coordinator's.

### Module boundaries

**One production module changes: `packages/configurator-domain/src/generation/generation-priorities.ts`.**

`PREFIX_WALL` becomes a derived pair — the **prefix** wall (the narrower) and the **suffix** wall (the
wider) — computed once per composition from the room and threaded to every site that today names a
wall letter for a layout reason. `chooseWallCut`'s feasibility lookups, `builtPlan`'s wall assignment,
`inSpatialOrder`, `slotsInReadingOrder`, `isLaidOutInReverse`, `firstStorageSlotAfterTheHob` and
`tallColumnItems`' id template all read it. **`floorWidthsMm`, `remainderMm` and `placeAlongRun` keep
physical wall keys** — they describe the room, not the layout, and nothing downstream may start
reading a role where it expects a wall.

**`leftover-rule.ts` does not change.** **`tall-end-rule.ts` changes by a rename and a comment
only**: `hobStandsOnWallA` is renamed to name the layout role it actually means, and the false sentence
at `:51-53` is corrected to say *the free end the layout leaves* instead of *wall A*. **No threshold,
no arithmetic and no body id in that module moves**, and a criterion says so.

**`shell-design.ts` does not change**, and this is worth stating because it looks as though it should:
the shell is tiled at the boundaries `floorWidthsMm` gives it, per wall, and those keys stay physical.

### Risks, ranked, with the reason for the rank visible

1. **The silent reversal.** Re-key `firstStorageSlotAfterTheHob` and miss `isLaidOutInReverse`, or the
   converse, and the drawer stands at the wrong end of the kitchen while **nothing in the repository
   goes red** — no count, width, remainder, cut, provenance or digest moves, and the baseline masks
   the one field that does (E7). **Ranked first because it is the only failure here that ships.**
   Criterion 7 is the whole control, and it is why the two must be one expression rather than two
   agreeing ones.
2. **The block's wall lands as an implementation detail.** 47 175 rooms gain a full-height block on
   wall B, and **the diff that does it reads as a refactor** — the behaviour falls out of the
   prefix/suffix re-keying with no line of code naming it. **The owner's ruling removes the question
   and does not remove this risk:** what ships is now authorised, but ADR 0110 Amendment E still says
   *"nowhere else"* until S1(a) amends it, and an implementer who never noticed the block moved will
   not notice the amendment is owed either. Criterion 10 and the S1(a)-before-S2 ordering are the
   control.
3. **The key silently becomes the free run**, because `chooseWallCut` already holds `capacities` and
   the room is one field further away. The result would be 100 / 100 on the wrong split and would read

4. **The baseline is re-measured instead of re-captured** — 7D4's own defect 5, repeated one wave
   later, with the plan that recorded it in front of the implementer. Criterion 11.
5. **The 14 335 sink exceptions get "fixed" by dropping the preparation cabinet** without Q-7D8-2
   being answered, turning a layout preference into a cabinet the customer does not get. Criterion 2's
   must-not.
6. ~~**The mirrored reading direction ships unasked**, quietly restating ADR 0110 A1's *"left to right

**Q-7D8-1 — ANSWERED (Ruling B above): the run reads the other way in the mirrored rooms.** *(Recorded

toward the corner and out along wall B. **The cabinets, the widths and the cooking sequence along the
run are identical; what changes is which end of the room the kitchen starts at.** Asked as a

gap in the run. **The plan is written for *keep the cabinet*.** Asked as a description: *in a medium
room, would you rather the sink sat round the corner from the hob, or the drawer unit between them

### Verification

`pnpm --filter @lemnaria/configurator-domain test` and the three-adapter parity suite per slice;
`pnpm check` before the wave's closing commit; `pnpm ci:local` before the push.

**And one gate this wave does not have, stated here because this is where a reader comes to learn what
verifies it: there is no automated gate on this plan itself.** `docs/` is in `.prettierignore`, so
`format` — the one gate that would otherwise read a markdown file — **skips it and reports success**.
**E0's banner carries the reproduction and the exact output.** Every slice of this wave edits this
file at close-out, and **the only thing that checks those edits is a person reading the diff.** A
close-out citing `pnpm ci:local` as evidence that its documentation is sound has cited a gate that
never opened the file.

**The sweep is the verification, and it is run twice.** Every criterion's close-out line is measured
against the **wave's own build** on the **10 mm** grid and **reports both arms of the split with the
population named and sized**; and the **50 mm** figures are reproduced alongside, so the wave's numbers
also sit in the denominator ADR 0120 C2 and ADR 0121 carry. **Each sweep figure carries its grid, its
ceiling, its population and its denominator. A criterion reported with an aggregate alone is not
reported** — an aggregate is what passed the broken code at 83.5 %.

**Two things this plan measured and one it did not, stated so the close-out is not read as wider
than it is.** Measured: every figure in E0–E8, from a scratch build at `8201915`. **Not measured: the
test suite was never run by this planning pass** — the tree was frozen for `ci:local` — so **no test
count is claimed anywhere above**, and R7's run-end-panel consequence is reasoned from source line
numbers rather than swept.

### 7D8 adjudication — S2's stop conditions, 2026-09-17

**Three findings were raised against slice S2 by the coordinator, two of them as candidate stop
conditions. The wave does not stop. None of the three is a defect in S2's code, and all three are
defects in this plan** — which is why the corrections above are edits to criteria rather than
instructions to an implementer.

**What this section rests on, labelled.** The S2 measurements below are **reported by the
implementer and were not re-run here** (this adjudication is markdown-only and did not build).
Everything drawn from this plan, ADR 0110, ADR 0093 and ADR 0121 is **doc-quoted**; the code
readings — `generation-priorities.ts`'s two `slotsInReadingOrder` call sites and its two
`isLaidOutInReverse` uses, `wallLengthMm`'s wall-to-dimension mapping, and
`drawer-rows.test.ts`'s `inReadingOrder` helper — are **source-verified in the working tree at
`355a15e` plus S2's uncommitted diff**. **The 74 of Finding A is the one figure that needed neither**:
it is arithmetic over E3's own published numbers.

#### Finding A — the 74 lost blocks: a defect of record, and the owner's ruling stands

**Classification: contract gap, in this plan and in ADR 0110 Amendment I1. Not an implementation
defect; no fix is assigned to any slice.**

**Ruled: the ruling stands and is corrected rather than re-put to the owner.** The owner chose
between an arm costing **74** and an arm costing **12 900**; the correction moves one side of a
174-fold comparison and reorders nothing. The 74 are a consequence of **E1's entered-length key**,
which was the architect's ruling and was never before the owner, and **the refused arm does not
avoid them**. Full reasoning, mechanism and witness: **ADR 0110 Amendment I1.1**, written
2026-09-17; the figure is corrected in E3, criterion 10 and Ruling A above.

**The owner is owed a notification, not a decision.** *"Nobody"* is a qualitative promise and it is
now false in 74 rooms; criterion 10 carries the obligation to say so at close-out, with the witness.

**On the coordinator's disclosure that they supplied the wrong figure: that is the reason to trust
this adjudication, not to discount it.** The correcting arithmetic — 12 900 − 12 826 = 74 — was
already printed in E3 beside the claim it refutes. **The failure was not measurement, it was
inferring a superset from a rising total**, and it is recorded in ADR 0110 I1.1 in that form so the
next reader inherits the lesson rather than the number.

#### Finding B — P6b is empty: the wave does not fail its own criterion, and the branch is kept

**Classification: contract gap (criterion 7 and E7 named a population that this wave's own criterion 1
dissolves) plus a test-fidelity problem (no declared witness for the arm that emptied). Not an
implementation defect.**

**B1 — the wave is not failing criterion 7 as the criterion is written.** Criterion 7's clause
*"names P6's size and fails if that arm is empty"* was written against a **P6 that this plan defined
as the physical wall-B arm** — *"the composed drawer slot stands on wall B"* — and **that arm is not
empty: it measures 5 910, exactly as planned, and criterion 8 reproduced it.** The clause is
therefore satisfiable on its own terms and is not the failure. **What has happened is worse than a
failed criterion: the criterion stopped referring to the thing it was written to protect**, because
*on wall B* and *reached through the prefix branch* were one set at HEAD and are two after the
re-key. The populations are now split into **P6a** and **P6b** above and the clause is replaced by
criteria **7a / 7b / 7c**.

**B2 — the prefix branch is UNREACHABLE under `APPROVED_ROOM_POLICY`, and that is not the same as
dead code.** It is reachable in the type: `firstStorageSlotAfterTheHob` is a total function of
`{hobStandsOnTheSuffixWall, slotCounts, walls}` and the branch executes whenever the first is false.
What makes it unenterable is an **empirical** fact about the admitted room range — criterion 1
holding with zero exceptions — and E5 already states the reason: the hob is the reading order's last
element, so it leaves the suffix wall only at `cut = kept.length`, *"and no room in the accepted
range does that."* **An empirical emptiness is a fact about the policy bounds, not about the rule.**

**B3 — RULED: the branch is KEPT. Deleting it is refused, for three independent reasons.**

1. **Deleting it edits 7D4's ruled behaviour, which this wave's own scope forbids.** ADR 0110
   Amendment H1 / ruling D15.7 rules *the first storage slot after the hob **in the reading order***.
   Collapsing the function to the suffix wall's first slot narrows that rule to *the first slot on
   the hob's own wall* — **the exact defect `drawer-rows.test.ts` was written to prevent**, and this
   plan's *goal* section forbids it in terms: *"the reading order itself … is untouched"*.
2. **It replaces a rule with a coincidence.** The branch is correct by construction; its emptiness is
   contingent on bounds that are **actively moving in this same milestone** — 7D6 derives the
   corner's reach from the cabinet depth and **7D7's Q-7D7-2 explicitly moves wall A's minimum**. A
   later widening that makes the population non-empty would, against a deleted branch, stand the
   drawer at the wrong end with **no count, width, remainder, cut, provenance or digest moving** —
   risk 1's failure, re-armed and with its control removed.
3. **ADR 0118 governs the converse and not this.** 0118 forbids *building* for a problem that has
   not occurred. This branch is not built for a future problem; it is **already-ruled behaviour whose
   discriminating population shrank**, and deleting shipped behaviour is not what 0118 asks for.

**B4 — ADR 0093 decision 1 applies, is not satisfied today, and is discharged by a declared witness
rather than by stopping the wave.** Decision 1 is unambiguous: *"a ruled behaviour that the tree
cannot distinguish from its own absence is unshipped."* **Today the tree cannot distinguish the
descending-index path from its absence, so that path is unshipped and the obligation is live.**
ADR 0093 **decision 2 and decision 3b supply the remedy for exactly this shape** — a consequence
*"not reachable from today's seed"* is witnessed by **a design the test declares** at the unit
boundary, with the test stating the unreachability and why. **That is criterion 7b, it is S3's, and
it is cheap.** Stopping the wave would leave the repository in the strictly worse state it is in
right now: the mirrored layout shipped in 82 395 rooms with **no** control at all.

**B5 — what is NOT unreachable, stated because the brief asked whether `isLaidOutInReverse` is dead
code. It is not, and calling it dead would be the most expensive error available here.**
`isLaidOutInReverse` has **two** uses. Its `slotsInReadingOrder` use has an unreachable true-arm;
its **`inSpatialOrder` use is live in all 82 395 P1 rooms** — it is the expression that mirrors the
kitchen, the whole visible subject of ADR 0110 Amendment I5. **Only the descending-slot path is
unwitnessed. The expression itself is heavily exercised and must stay one expression** (risk 1).

#### Finding C — the sabotage results are real, and one of them was taken against an invalid control

**Classification: test-fidelity problem, and the control criterion 7 names has not been built yet
because S3 has not run. This is the expected state after S2, not a regression.**

**C1 — the 25 → 21 result is not evidence that the repository cannot catch the inversion; it is
evidence that it cannot catch it *today*, and the reason is diagnosed.** A sabotage measured against
a **25-red suite is not a measurement** — the control is not in a state where a red can be
attributed. The four tests that turn green are diagnosable from source:
`packages/configurator-domain/tests/generation/drawer-rows.test.ts:64-71` re-derives the reading
order as `[...alongTheWall(plan, "B")].reverse(), ...alongTheWall(plan, "A")` — **the test's own
model of the reversal, hard-coded to wall B.** That helper is the test-side twin of
`isLaidOutInReverse`, and it is now stale. Reverting production to `wall === "B"` makes production
agree with the stale model again, which is why four go green. **The repository is not rewarding the
defect; it is rewarding agreement with a fixture this wave invalidated**, and the distinction decides
the repair.

**C2 — RULED: the repair is to re-derive the test's reading order from the entered wall lengths, and
that is a STRENGTHENING.** The file's header states its design intent in its own words — this file
and `generation-priorities.ts` *"agree only if both read wall B's reversal the same way"*. **That
independence is the asset and it must survive**: the helper is re-keyed **from the room**, never by
importing production's `isLaidOutInReverse` or by reading a planned id. A repair that imports the
production helper turns an independent oracle into a tautology and is a finding, not a fix.

**C3 — the 25 → 25 result is the serious one and it is not explained.** Leaving the slot lookup on
the literals `"B"` / `"A"` changes which wall the drawer is sought on in every P1 room — the suffix
call becomes `("A", slotCounts.A)` where it should read wall B — and **nothing measured it.** The
prefix call is unreachable, so only the second literal bites, and it bites in 82 395 rooms.
**S3 must make criterion 7c go red under this sabotage specifically**, and must report the count
rather than the pass.

**C4 — risk 1's control is not "removed"; it was never built.** This plan assigns it to **S3** —
*"criterion 7's dedicated guard, the whole-recorded witnesses … and a sabotage run in both
directions"*. **S2 shipping without it is the plan working.** What Finding C changes is that S3 is
now **load-bearing for the wave rather than confirmatory**, and it must run against a green suite.

#### Sequencing — the plain answer

**S2 may be committed as it stands, and the commit must not be pushed.** Four things make that safe,
each checked rather than assumed:

- **Criterion 10's surviving must-not is satisfied.** *"No commit puts a column on wall B before
  S1(a)'s amendment has landed."* S1(a) landed at **`2439da5`**, which is an ancestor of HEAD
  **`355a15e`**. **[verified by `git log`]** The repository is no longer shipping against its own
  record.
- **The record is true before the code lands.** ADR 0110 Amendment I1.1 and this plan's corrections
  are written now, ahead of the commit, so the 74 is not discovered after the fact.
- **`--no-verify` is permitted on intermediate commits** (`docs/WORKFLOW.md`, step 6, owner's
  direction 2026-08-26) and **the commit message must name the 25 red tests and assign them to S3**.
  A commit made this way *"may not be described as verified"* — say so.
- **`docs/WORKFLOW.md`'s pre-push rule is absolute: a red build must not reach GitHub.** **So S3
  lands before any push, and no reviewer is dispatched until the suite is green** (QA gates review).

**May S3 touch the two files whose arm-coverage floors now measure 0? YES — and the distinction the
brief asks for is real, so here it is in the only form that is safe to act on.**

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `drawer-rows.test.ts:313`, `arms.wallB >= 30` | drawer slots on **physical wall B** (P6a) | **The population did not empty — 5 910 rooms still qualify.** The count is computed *through* the stale `inReadingOrder` helper, so what reads 0 is the instrument, not the arm. | **Repair the helper. The floor itself must NOT be lowered, and 30 is a floor rather than a target.** Once the helper is re-keyed this arm must be non-zero again; **if it is not, that is a finding and S3 stops.** |
| any floor on P6b — the reversed / `count − 1` arm | slots reached through the **prefix branch** | **The population genuinely emptied**, 6 660 → 0, by criterion 1 (Finding B). | **Must NOT be lowered to 0, and must NOT be deleted.** It is **re-sited**: the arm moves from a sweep floor to criterion **7b**'s declared unit witness, and the sweep-side assertion is replaced by an explicit statement that the arm is unreachable from `APPROVED_ROOM_POLICY` and why (ADR 0093 decision 3b's construction). **Coverage is moved, never dropped.** |

**The governing rule, so the two are never confused again: a floor that reads 0 because the
instrument is stale is repaired; a floor that reads 0 because the population emptied is re-sited to
a declared witness. Neither is ever relaxed to 0.** ADR 0091 Amendment A binds — **no assertion of
7D4's rule may be weakened by this wave** — and criterion 8 already says so.

**Ownership: both files are S3's, and S3 alone.** S2's diff stays a pure re-key so criterion 5's
zero-field-difference result remains reviewable as one unit. **S2 must not green its own stale
assertions**, which is the shape QA exists to separate.
